title_ru: Fallout 3 — F3DAD: наследование actor templates, эффективный инвентарь и археология закрытых/отброшенных Vault-компонентов
title_en: Fallout 3 — F3DAD Actor-Template Inheritance / ACBS Effective Inventory & Closed-Vault Archaeology Audit v1.6

format_semantics.tpl_extension: NPC_ TPLT may resolve to NPC_ or LVLN; CREA TPLT may resolve to CREA or LVLC.
format_semantics.inventory_semantics: When ACBS Use Inventory (0x0100) is set, effective inventory is resolved from the actor template recursively. Levelled templates are represented conservatively as branch unions rather than deterministic inventory rolls.
format_semantics.fo3_outfit_normalization: For this audit, player-visible actor clothing/weapons are evaluated through effective CNTO inventory inheritance; no separate FO3 OTFT outfit record is assumed.

actor_pipeline: compute explicit CNTO versus effective inventory
re-evaluate low raw-use items under effective actor exposure
vault_pipeline: scan CELL EDID/FULL for Vault families
add active MoveTo targets as conservative alternate ingress
split each numbered Vault into connected components
inspect detached interior components separately from exterior layout revision cells
compare OLD/x/NEW named exterior construction cells against production siblings

findings.result: Low direct-use counts can substantially understate how widely an actor weapon/effect is exposed once Use Inventory inheritance and levelled actor templates are expanded.
findings.claim_boundary: Effective list-template inventory is a conservative branch union; the registry does not claim every branch item appears on every runtime spawn.

findings.result: No rare item was found whose meaningful obtainability is created solely by a reachable actor inheriting Use Inventory from a statically unreachable actor template.
findings.meaning: v1.5 negative result survives recursive template inheritance; no secret item claim is manufactured from actor-template plumbing.

only_xtel_pair: REFR 00036C33 in Vault106bHall -> REFR 00036E9E in Vault106bDorms
findings.interpretation: A sparse two-cell living-quarters blockout survived detached from the production Vault 106 graph. Its two cells link only to each other, while the production living quarters are consolidated into the much denser Vault106b cell. This supports a superseded layout/revision interpretation, not a hidden accessible room claim.
findings.public_status: Vault106bDorms and Vault106bHall are publicly marked as cut content; the primary contribution here is the exact disconnected XTEL component and density comparison.

public_footprint.registry_contribution: Exact shipped XTEL isolation, ref/door density and comparison against production Vault106b.

findings.public_status: Public Fallout documentation already identifies Vault101Demo as an inaccessible test/demo version used for press/demo purposes.
findings.research_role: Positive control proving that the vault-access graph correctly recognizes a truly isolated but already documented demo/test interior.

selected_content_differences.xVault87OLD: 113 refs dominated by canyon rocks/trees; no door or Vault interior connection.
selected_content_differences.xVault87ExtOLD: 116 refs including 3 super-mutant creature placements and mutant-camp dressing; adjacent grid to final Vault87Ext.
selected_content_differences.Vault87Ext: 132 refs with radiation markers/dust, dead scientist, Rad-X/RadAway and cave dressing.
selected_content_differences.xVault92ExteriorOLD: 64 refs, almost entirely terrain/trees plus a monorail static.
selected_content_differences.Vault92Ext: 109 refs including cave-entrance statics and ambient falling-rock/dust FX.
selected_content_differences.Vault112Exterior: 162 refs dominated by road chunks, rocks and generic junk.
selected_content_differences.Vault112ExteriorNEW: 215 refs with the Smith Casey/gas-station/industrial exterior dressing; public technical documentation uses this NEW cell as the production Smith Casey entrance area.

findings.interpretation: The shipped Wasteland retains multiple explicitly OLD/NEW or x-prefixed exterior construction cells around Vault locations. They are exterior world-layout revisions rather than hidden Vault interiors. Exact chronology is admitted only where naming/public production use provides a comparator (strongest for Vault112Exterior -> Vault112ExteriorNEW and explicit *OLD names).

findings.result: No additional numbered Vault interior CELL family was found in the six supplied shipped masters under the inspected CELL EDID/FULL corpus. This does not rule out lore-only Vault references, deleted pre-release assets absent from the shipped masters, or unnamed generic Vault-kit cells.

what_bethesda_appears_to_have_abandoned: a sparse two-cell Vault 106 living-quarters layout later replaced by the dense production Vault106b architecture
multiple exterior construction/location revisions around Vault 87/92/112, and likely Vault 108, with the strongest explicit comparator being Vault112Exterior versus Vault112ExteriorNEW
Vault101Demo as a deliberately non-production demo/test slice rather than a hidden story Vault
what_is_not_claimed: the exact reason Bethesda cut/replaced any layout
that OLD/x exterior cells are inaccessible gameplay interiors
that any additional numbered Vault exists in these shipped masters
that a template-inherited rare item is a new obtainable secret

public_footprint_controls.note: The cut labels are public; v1.6 contributes the primary ESM component graph.

public_footprint_controls.subject: Vault112ExteriorNEW
public_footprint_controls.note: Public Vault 112 / Smith Casey technical data uses Vault112ExteriorNEW as the production entrance-area cell.

claim_ceiling: Use Inventory inheritance is resolved statically from TPLT plus ACBS Template Flags; levelled templates are represented as branch unions, not deterministic inventory rolls.
No actor-template item is called secret solely from low raw CNTO/use counts.
A disconnected interior CELL is not automatically a new numbered Vault; naming, topology and production comparators are required.
Exterior cells with OLD/x/NEW names are development-layout evidence, not inaccessible interior Vaults.
No exact Bethesda design reason is inferred from static assets; only superseded/incomplete implementation evidence is claimed.
Community/public footprint checks are used only to prevent rediscovery claims; primary asset graph remains the authority for static relationships.

next_gate.goal: Resolve OLD/x/NEW Vault exterior cells against world coordinates, NAVM connectivity, map markers, entrance doors and production encounter geography; determine which are merely named landscape cells versus true superseded entrance-location layouts.
next_gate.secondary_goal: Audit detached Vault106bHall/Dorms NAVM and geometry adjacency to determine whether an unlinked portal/door was deleted or whether the pair was abandoned before integration.
